compiled_state.title: merge-to-main-pr.sh: PR1 staged-intermediate lacks auto-merge while wait-for-pr awaits MERGED -> deadlock to 30min timeout
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Incident Overview

**Symptom:** In the non-sprint two-tier merge path, `_phase_staged_intermediate` creates PR1 (feature -> staged-*) with a plain `gh pr create` (no auto-merge), then calls `wait-for-pr.sh $_pr1_number` to wait for checks. But `wait-for-pr.sh` only exits 0 on terminal state MERGED (it classifies all-checks-green-but-OPEN as PENDING and keeps polling). The script's own merge step (`gh pr merge --merge`) runs AFTER that wait returns. So nothing ever merges PR1: wait-for-pr.sh polls until its 30-min timeout, exits 1, and the script aborts ('refusing to advance to PR2').

**Contrast:** PR2's `_phase_merge` does NOT have this bug — it queues `gh pr merge $_pr_number --auto --merge` (line ~1275) right after PR creation, so GitHub auto-merges when checks pass and wait-for-pr.sh observes MERGED.

**Observed:** Live on PR1 #536 during the fp3-only -> main integration on 2026-06-02. PR1 reached all-checks-green + mergeStateStatus=CLEAN + autoMergeRequest=null, and the merge script sat in 'waiting for PR1 #536 required checks to complete...' indefinitely. Manually running `gh pr merge 536 --merge` unblocked it (wait-for-pr.sh then saw MERGED and the script advanced to PR2).

**code_version:** 7f406df621

**Proposed fix:** Queue auto-merge on PR1 immediately after creation in `_phase_staged_intermediate`, mirroring `_phase_merge` (`gh pr merge $_pr1_number --auto --merge`). Step 5's existing 'if state != MERGED then merge' guard remains as a fallback for repos without auto-merge enabled.
